finding.problem: Fixture commit C3 has checks_passed true but no checked_at. The new checks-pass precondition requires exists(target.checked_at), so C3 can no longer be approved, although its fixture shows it as having passed its check. C1 is already approved and also has no checked_at. The fixtures were not updated to match the new property.
finding.where: SKILL.md, Authoring World (fixtures): Commits C1 and C3; Commit.checked_at

findings.label: seeded
findings.why: Existing commits such as the already-approved C1 and the passed C3 have no checked_at, so they are treated as having no fresh check. That is the breakage of past behavior for commits approved on old checks.

finding.problem: record_approval is a kernel reply that arrives after the kernel has already merged the commit into main. Its approved-only-if-checked precondition now depends on the clock. A check that is 23h59m old when approve_commit is taken can be over a day old when the reply is recorded, so the record is refused after the merge has happened. The recorded state then disagrees with main.

findings.label: other-real
findings.why: record_approval is a reply that arrives after the merge, so the clock-dependent precondition can refuse it near the one-day boundary. That is a genuine race, but not the seeded past-behavior breakage.

finding.problem: The invariant approved-commits-passed-their-checks still tests only checks_passed. It does not reflect the new freshness rule, so a stale or missing checked_at is not covered. Its reason text and the glossary entry for 'change check' also say nothing about the one-day limit. Meanwhile checks_passed stays true after the check expires, so the commit still reads as checked wherever that field is used alone.

findings.label: other-real
findings.why: The invariant approved-commits-passed-their-checks still tests only checks_passed and ignores freshness, and checks_passed stays true after expiry. This is a real inconsistency, but it is not the seeded problem.

finding.problem: The new expressions use `now`, `1 day` and a `timestamp` type, none of which is used or defined anywhere else in the skill. The examples have no case showing that a check older than a day is denied by `checks-pass`, or that re-running check_commit refreshes checked_at. Also, check_commit is denied once a commit is approved (not-approved), so the 'run it again' advice in the checks-pass reason only works for unapproved commits.
finding.where: SKILL.md, Preconditions: approve_commit checks-pass; EXAMPLES.md approve-only-after-a-passing-check

findings.label: other-real
findings.why: The `now`, `1 day` and timestamp vocabulary is not defined elsewhere, there are no examples for the stale case, and the 'run it again' advice cannot work once a commit is approved. These are real but minor gaps, and none is the seeded one.

edit.why: It adds checked_at, sets it in record_check, and gates approval on a check less than a day old, which does what the request asked even though the invariant text was left unchanged.
